newsitem.title: UK: Harrods manager convicted of defrauding customers.
newsitem.headline: Harrods manager convicted of defrauding customers.

text.p: An employee at Harrods, London's luxury department store, was convicted on Monday of stealing more than 200,000 pounds ($335,000) from customer credit card accounts.
Elizabeth Johns, a 31-year old manager with the store, and her brother, Koshy, were refused bail and held in custody until sentencing next month.

During the five-day trial the jury was told that the Indian-born Johns took receipts from Harrods, identified high-spending customers and then, with the help of accomplices, encoded the details on to bogus Visa and Mastercard accounts.
One wealthy and unobservant customer's account was billed 120,000 pounds in just three months before the fraud was uncovered.
"He was a gold mine for the fraudsters," said prosecutor Michael Holland. "He seemed to have an almost bottomless credit card limit."
A total of 70 customer accounts were cloned and their accounts were plundered.
"Harrods have up to 5,000 employees at any one time and this case is a very rare one, thankfully," a spokesman for the store said.
"The overwhelming majority of our staff are both honest and very hard working and they are as appalled as Harrods itself by the way a trusted member of staff has let everyone down ($1=.5974 Pound)
